pages.name: Component ownership
pages.description_html:
Component ownership

Node Runtime owner: {owner}. Resource Allocation owner: {owner}.

The component owner reviews rollout risk, confirms the rollback plan, and coordinates follow-up work. Individual tickets carry their own assignee and due date. Code changes still need an authorized repository reviewer.

Fictional company scenario in a dedicated demo workspace.

pages.name: ADR-001: Bound graceful shutdown to five seconds
pages.description_html:
ADR-001: Bounded cancellation

Context. Shutdown can hang while outstanding requests wait for a stalled dependency. Waiting indefinitely delays deployments and leaves old processes consuming capacity.

Decision: use bounded cancellation with a five second shutdown deadline. Stop accepting new work, allow active requests to drain, then cancel outstanding work when the deadline expires.

Tradeoff. Some requests may be cancelled instead of completing. Callers must tolerate cancellation and retry only operations that are safe to repeat.

Rollout. Start with a canary and retain a manual rollback checkpoint. API approval alone does not approve operational readiness.

Fictional demo ADR.

pages.name: Runbook: Runtime canary and rollback
pages.description_html:
Runtime canary and rollback

Before rollout. Confirm cancellation is enabled, record shutdown latency, and identify the operator responsible for rollback.

Rollback trigger. Pause rollout when shutdown latency exceeds five seconds in the canary, or when cancelled requests continue consuming capacity.

Procedure. Stop the next rollout stage, restore the previous runtime configuration, and verify that request draining has recovered. Keep the incident ticket open until the operator records the result.

Fictional demo runbook.

pages.name: ADR-002: Preserve reservations during resize retries
pages.description_html:
ADR-002: Reservation fairness

Context. A failed resize can retry ahead of queued reservations. Repeated retries may keep existing customers waiting even when capacity becomes available.

Decision: preserve existing reservations and retry resize automatically at most twice. Reservations keep their queue position; a failed resize must stop after its second automatic retry.

Reason. Unlimited retries can starve existing reservations. A retry cap limits repeated work but does not prove that reservation fairness is fixed.

Open risk. The starvation replay has not been completed. Keep the concern open and block expansion beyond the canary until that evidence is available.

Fictional demo ADR.

pages.name: Runbook: Allocation rollback and reservation checks
pages.description_html:
Allocation rollback

Watch. Track queued reservation age, resize retry count, and reservations completed during the canary.

Rollback trigger. Rollback resize if reservation starvation is observed or queue order changes after a retry.

Procedure. Pause the allocation rollout, disable automatic resize retries, and keep existing reservations in order. The component owner checks queue recovery before restarting the rollout.

Evidence. Record the affected reservation, retry count, rollback time, and recovery result in the rollout ticket.

Fictional demo runbook.

pages.name: RFC: Resize retry options and fairness
pages.description_html:
Resize retry alternatives

Immediate retry. We considered immediate retry to recover transient failures quickly. It remains an option to evaluate; we have not rejected it.

Unlimited retry. We rejected unlimited retry because it can starve existing reservations and keep failed work ahead of queued customers.

Bounded retry. The current ADR allows at most two automatic retries while preserving reservation order. Compare recovery rate and oldest reservation age before changing that policy.

Next evidence. Run a reservation starvation replay with concurrent resize failures. Document the result before requesting wider rollout.

Fictional demo RFC.

items.name: Bound graceful shutdown
items.description_html:
Stop accepting new work during shutdown and cancel outstanding requests when the five-second deadline expires.

Acceptance: request draining stops at the deadline; cancelled work releases capacity; the timeout is configurable.

comments.comment_html: I am concerned that shutdown can exceed the five second deadline when a dependency stops responding. Please include stalled requests in the cancellation replay.

I confirm the shutdown deadline concern is resolved after the bounded cancellation test. In the simulated 200-request replay, pending requests were cancelled within the five-second deadline. Keep the canary rollback check in place.

items.name: Measure cancellation overhead
items.description_html:
Compare request latency and capacity release before and after bounded cancellation.

Acceptance: record the replay settings, latency distribution, and remaining active requests. Separate cancellation behavior from normal request completion.

comments.comment_html: The prototype adds a cancellation check to each active request. Measure that overhead separately from the time saved during shutdown.
Use the same request mix for both runs. Keep a manual rollback checkpoint before expanding the canary.

items.name: Document runtime rollback
items.description_html:
Write an operator checklist for reverting bounded cancellation if the runtime canary regresses.

Acceptance: name the rollback trigger, configuration to restore, and verification needed before resuming rollout.

comments.comment_html: The runbook needs a step to confirm cancelled requests have released capacity. A configuration rollback alone is not enough.
The API review covered naming only. Please get a separate operational review of the rollback steps.

items.name: Verify shutdown deadline
items.description_html:
Exercise slow dependencies and stalled request handlers against the five-second shutdown deadline.

Acceptance: retain the scenario inputs and cancellation results, including requests that do not complete normally.

comments.comment_html: I approve only the API naming. That does not approve the reliability behavior or remove the canary requirement.
The runtime ADR now specifies when draining ends and cancellation begins. Use that sequence in the test checklist.

items.name: Confirm runtime review routing
items.description_html:
Confirm who reviews runtime rollout risk and who checks the rollback procedure.

Acceptance: the owner and review route are documented; repository approval is requested separately for code changes.

comments.comment_html: Please request a peer review of the rollback checklist. The person implementing the change should not be its only reviewer.
Include the Capacity team when the cancellation change affects reservation cleanup. The shared failure case needs coverage.

items.name: Track runtime canary rollout
items.description_html:
Record the runtime canary checkpoint and the decision to pause, continue, or roll back.

Acceptance: attach the cancellation replay, rollback checklist, and operator sign-off before wider rollout.

comments.comment_html: Keep the rollout paused until the rollback checklist has an operational review.
The shutdown replay does not cover reservation starvation. Allocation needs its own test before its rollout can expand.

items.name: Cap resize retries at two
items.description_html:
Implement the allocation ADR: preserve existing reservation order and stop after two automatic resize retries.

Acceptance: a third automatic attempt is prevented; reservations retain their position; operators can see why retries stopped.

comments.comment_html: I am concerned that resize retry can starve existing reservations. The retry cap is useful, but we still need a replay showing queued reservations continue to make progress.
The two-retry patch is ready for review. It does not resolve the starvation concern until the reservation replay is complete.

items.name: Measure reservation progress during retries
items.description_html:
Replay concurrent resize failures while reservations are queued. Compare oldest reservation age and completed reservations with retries enabled and disabled.

Acceptance: retain the replay settings and results; identify whether any existing reservation stops making progress.

comments.comment_html: No starvation replay result is attached yet. Please keep that risk open even if the retry patch merges.
Link the replay result from the allocation rollout ticket so the release review can find it.

items.name: Document allocation rollback
items.description_html:
Document how to pause allocation rollout and disable resize retries without changing reservation order.

Acceptance: include the trigger, operator steps, queue recovery check, and evidence to record after rollback.

comments.comment_html: Immediate retry is still an option under evaluation. The rejected option is unlimited retry; please keep those separate in the rollout summary.

items.name: Verify isolation between resize and reservations
items.description_html:
Check that repeated resize failures cannot consume the capacity reserved for existing requests.

Acceptance: reservations retain their allocation and queue position while resize work reaches its retry cap.

comments.comment_html: Add a rollback case where a failed resize is paused while existing reservations remain queued. We need to verify recovery order.

items.name: Confirm allocation escalation owner
items.description_html:
Record who owns allocation rollout risk and who receives reservation starvation escalations.

Acceptance: the ownership page names the responsible owner and the rollout ticket names its assignee.

comments.comment_html: Use the component ownership page for escalation. Assigning this ticket does not transfer responsibility for the whole service.

items.name: Track allocation canary readiness
items.description_html:
Collect the retry policy, reservation replay, and rollback plan for the allocation release review.

Acceptance: the owner records a rollout decision after reviewing all three. Keep unresolved starvation evidence visible.

comments.comment_html: Completing the release checklist must not automatically close the reservation starvation concern. It needs its own resolution evidence.

messages: Shutdown is hanging when a dependency stops responding. Can we put a hard deadline on draining requests?
Use a five-second shutdown deadline, then cancel the remaining work. I have written that policy into the ADR.
Please include stalled requests in the replay. Timing out the process is not enough if the work keeps consuming capacity.
The simulated cancellation replay now finishes within five seconds. The shutdown deadline concern is resolved; the canary check stays in place.
Keep the rollback trigger on shutdown latency and verify that cancelled requests release capacity.
The cancellation API naming looks good. Does that mean we are ready to roll out?
API naming is approved. That approval does not cover reliability or the operational rollout.
We still need an operational review of the rollback checklist before expanding the canary.
I added a check that cancelled requests have released capacity after rollback. Please review that step.
Agreed. Keep the rollout paused until that review is recorded.
Resize retries can keep queued reservations waiting. Can we cap retries before the allocation rollout?
The policy is now at most two automatic retries, with existing reservations keeping their queue position.
The cap limits repeated work, but it does not prove reservations cannot starve.
The starvation replay is still missing. Please test queued reservations alongside repeated resize failures.
Keep the concern open and hold expansion beyond the canary until those results are available.
The rollout summary says immediate retry was rejected. Is that what we agreed?
No. Immediate retry was considered and is still an option to evaluate.
Unlimited retry was rejected because it can starve existing reservations. That is a different option.
I will correct the summary to distinguish the two. The current decision remains bounded retry.
Compare recovery rate and oldest reservation age in the replay before proposing another policy change.
Who should review the allocation rollback plan before we expand the canary?
{owner} owns Resource Allocation and should review the rollout risk. We still need a separate authorized reviewer for code changes.
The rollback plan pauses resize retries and preserves reservation order. Please check the queue recovery step.
Also record the affected reservation, retry count, and recovery result in the rollout ticket.
Do not treat that checklist review as resolution of the starvation concern. We still need the replay result.
Can we expand the runtime canary after the shutdown replay?
Only after the operator has reviewed the rollback checklist and confirmed the cancellation deadline.
The rollback trigger is shutdown latency above five seconds or cancelled work continuing to hold capacity.
Please attach the replay and operator review to the rollout ticket so the release review has both.
Allocation remains a separate release decision. Its reservation starvation test is still outstanding.
